body:
## Summary

- **Covering indexes** for `host`, `latestApiEndpoint`, `category/subCategory` on `malicious_events` — eliminates 661K document fetches per query, switching plans from `IXSCAN→FETCH` to `DISTINCT_SCAN` with `docsExamined=0`
- **`ParallelQueryExecutor`** utility to run independent Mongo queries concurrently — reusable across all dashboard APIs
- **`fetchAlertFilters`** refactored to run all 4 distinct queries in parallel instead of sequentially
- **`DashboardFilterCache`** — in-process cache with day-bucketed keys and configurable TTL (`DASHBOARD_FILTER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, default 300s). Caches `fetchAlertFilters` response and `listMaliciousRequests` count

## Benchmark results (localhost, N=50 C=10)

| API | Before p50 | After p50 | Before p90 | After p90 | Before p95 | After p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fetchFiltersThreatTable | 4.45s | 0.82s | 7.26s | 0.83s | — | — |
| fetchSuspectSampleData | 1477ms | 53ms | 2195ms | 81ms | 2195ms | 86ms |

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify `fetchFiltersThreatTable` returns correct filter values (actors, hosts, urls, subCategories)
- [ ] Verify `fetchSuspectSampleData` returns correct count and 50 samples
- [ ] Verify cache invalidates after TTL (set `DASHBOARD_FILTER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=5` and confirm stale data refreshes)

feat: add self-healing scan backpressure breaker to guardrails-service
body:
Port agent-guard's LatencyBreaker to guardrails-service. A rolling, time-bounded latency circuit breaker watches the downstream scan path (ProcessRequest/ResponseParallel -> agent-guard /scan). When the recent average latency crosses GUARDRAILS_BACKPRESSURE_AVG_LATENCY_MS (default 8000ms), ValidateRequest/ValidateResponse fail-open (Allowed) instead of blocking on the slow dependency, preserving throughput while it recovers.

Latency is recorded on both success and error so a string of agent-guard timeouts trips the breaker and sheds load fast rather than each request waiting out the 60s HTTP timeout. Self-heals via TTL eviction (per-process state). GET /backpressure exposes the live snapshot for diagnostics.

perf: run agent-guard services with multiple uvicorn workers
body:
The worker ran a single uvicorn process, pinning the cache-serve path to one core (~63 rps/instance, measured) while the other 7 cores on the n2-standard-8 box sat idle — the real per-instance throughput ceiling for high-RPM traffic. Run one worker per core (UVICORN_WORKERS, default $(nproc)); the worker is stateless (all state in Redis) so workers parallelize cleanly. ~8x per instance.

Also give the embedder and anonymizer multiple workers for the cache-miss CPU path, and pin torch/BLAS to one thread per embedder worker so N workers don't each spawn nproc compute threads and oversubscribe the CPU.

title: fix: make cascade backpressure self-healing + serve cache before back…
body:
…pressure

cascade_backpressure could latch ON permanently: once the rolling average of cascade latencies tripped the threshold, every request skipped the cascade, so no new latency was ever recorded — the count-based window never evicted the stale high samples and the average stayed above threshold until the process restarted. Result: guardrails silently fail-open indefinitely after any transient Vertex slowdown.

Make the latency window time-bounded: samples older than AGW_CASCADE_BACKPRESSURE_TTL_SECONDS (default 30s) are evicted on every read/write, independent of new traffic. Stale samples now age out, the window empties, the next cascade runs as a natural probe, and fresh latencies decide whether to re-trip — so a transient slowdown self-clears within ~TTL.

Also reorder scan_handler to consult the semantic cache BEFORE applying backpressure, so a cached verdict (including a cached block) is still served correctly while Vertex is slow; backpressure now only short-circuits a genuine cache miss.

Adds tests/test_cascade_backpressure.py (7 tests incl. the self-heal regression).

body:
Hi! 

Trying to use the open-source self-hosted dashboard, and I'm not sure if I'm missing a config step. After signing up and logging in, the dashboard shows "Access Restricted / Contact Sales" instead of the API Inventory. Wanted to ask whether the dashboard is meant to be fully usable on local_deploy, and if so, what I'm missing.

**Setup**
- Images:        aktosecurity/akto-api-security-dashboard:2.8.5_local,
  aktosecurity/akto-api-testing:2.8.5_local, 
  mongo:6.0.28

**What happens**
- Admin signs up at /signup, logs in fine, routes to /dashboard/... → then "Access Restricted".

**What I found while poking around (could easily be misreading it)**
- The SPA gate in `main/index.js` grants access when `window.PLAN_TYPE ∈ {enterprise, professional, trial}`.
- On a fresh local_deploy login, `window.PLAN_TYPE === ""` while `window.DASHBOARD_MODE === "LOCAL_DEPLOY", and the gate doesn't seem to look at DASHBOARD_MODE.

**Questions**
1. Is the dashboard intended to work on open-source local_deploy?
2. If so, is there a supported env/config to set the plan (so the gate passes), or anything I've skipped in the self-hosted setup?
3. If not expected, happy to file a proper issue with full repro.

Thanks for any pointers! 🙏

title: supress 403 and fix access display bug in api inventory
OpenAPI 3.1 specs import not supported — importer appears to only handle Swagger 2.0 / OpenAPI 3.0.x
body:
## Describe the bug

Importing a valid **OpenAPI 3.1.0** spec (dashboard → API Collections → import OpenAPI / `importDataFromOpenApiSpec`) creates the collection but populates **0 endpoints**, with no error surfaced in the UI. The same spec downgraded to OpenAPI 3.0.3 imports all endpoints correctly. It looks like the bundled swagger-parser doesn't handle the 3.1 JSON-Schema dialect and fails silently.

## To reproduce

1. Take any valid OpenAPI **3.1.0** document with a non-trivial number of paths.
2. Import it into a new collection via the dashboard (or `POST /api/importDataFromOpenApiSpec`).
3. Open the collection → it shows **0 endpoints**. No parse error is shown.
4. Edit the same document: change `openapi: 3.1.0` → `openapi: 3.0.3` (and remove the top-level `webhooks` object, which is 3.1-only).
5. Re-import → all endpoints now appear.

## Expected behavior

A valid OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec should import its endpoints (OpenAPI 3.1 has been stable since 2021). At minimum, an unparseable/unsupported spec should surface a clear error instead of silently importing 0 endpoints.

## Environment

- Self-hosted local deploy (`DASHBOARD_MODE=local_deploy`, MongoDB)
- Dashboard image: `aktosecurity/akto-api-security-dashboard:2.8.1_local`
- Testing image: `aktosecurity/akto-api-testing:2.8.0_local`
- Host: macOS / Docker Desktop

## Notes

- The source spec used had only two 3.1-specific markers: the `openapi` version string and a top-level `webhooks` object (no `type: [..]` nullable arrays, no `const`, no `jsonSchemaDialect`), so the blocker appears to be the version/dialect itself rather than exotic 3.1 features.
- Two possible fixes: (a) upgrade the bundled `swagger-parser` to a 3.1-capable version, and/or (b) emit a visible error when an import yields 0 endpoints so the failure isn't silent.

## Workaround

Down-convert the spec to 3.0.3 (bump `openapi`, strip `webhooks`) before importing.

Support MongoDB 7.x/8.x — server is effectively pinned to 6.0 by mongodb-driver-sync 4.2.1
body:
### Summary

The self-hosted Akto stack is effectively pinned to **MongoDB 6.0** because the
bundled MongoDB Java driver is **`mongodb-driver-sync` 4.2.1** (released Nov 2020),
which predates MongoDB 6.0/7.0/8.0 and does not officially support them. This blocks
operators from running a currently-supported MongoDB server (8.x) and raises the
security concerns below. Please consider upgrading the driver and the shipped MongoDB
version.

### Where the version is constrained today

- **MongoDB Java driver pin → `mongodb-driver-sync` 4.2.1**
  https://github.com/akto-api-security/akto/blob/master/apps/dashboard/pom.xml#L95-L96
  ```xml
  <artifactId>mongodb-driver-sync</artifactId>
  <version>4.2.1</version>
Canonical Docker Compose ships MongoDB 6.0
https://github.com/akto-api-security/akto/blob/master/docker-compose.yml#L7
image: mongo:6.0.1
Per the MongoDB driver↔server compatibility tables, the 4.2 driver line targets
server versions up to ~5.0; 6.0/7.0/8.0 require newer drivers (5.2+ for 8.0):
https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/compatibility/

Security concerns
End-of-life server. MongoDB 6.0 is beyond the end of life per MongoDB's support
lifecycle (https://www.mongodb.com/legal/support-policy/lifecycles). Running an
EOL server means no further security patches — unacceptable for security-tooling
deployments and a likely audit/compliance finding (SOC 2, ISO 27001, eIDAS, etc.).
Very old client driver. mongodb-driver-sync 4.2.1 is ~5 years old and misses
years of driver-side security and TLS fixes.

Missing modern security features. Staying on 6.0/4.2.1 forecloses newer MongoDB
security capabilities (e.g. improvements to TLS/OCSP, in-use encryption / Queryable
Encryption, and auditing) that security-conscious operators may require.
Unsupported-by-design pairing. The shipped 4.2.1 driver against even 6.0 is
already one major beyond its official matrix; this "works by backward compat" posture
is fragile and undocumented for operators who must certify their stack.

Proposed change
Upgrade mongodb-driver-sync to a 5.2+ release that supports MongoDB 8.0.
Bump the canonical docker-compose.yml (and any deployment manifests) to a supported
MongoDB server (8.0 LTS, or at minimum a non-EOL 7.0).
Validate startup, account/RBAC init, test-run orchestration, and the testing engine
against the new server, and document the supported MongoDB version range.

Environment / context
Self-hosted local_deploy stack (dashboard + testing + mongo + puppeteer-replay).
Observed downstream: integrators pinning mongo:6.0.x solely to match the driver.

## Summary

This PR adds tree view visualization for API endpoints in the inventory page — both GraphQL and REST collections.

### GraphQL Tree View

- Groups endpoints by URL structure: `operationType → fieldName → operationName`

### REST Tree View
- New **"Display tree view"** option for non-GraphQL collections

title: build combined api info and sti view and use it for posture page queries
body:
## Summary

Introduces a **materialized view** (`endpoint_info_views`) that pre-joins `api_info` with `single_type_info` data, replacing expensive real-time aggregations on the posture/inventory pages.

### Architecture

**Background cron** (`EndpointInfoViewCron`) runs every 10 minutes, **only on accounts with `enableEndpointInfoView` flag enabled**:

1. **Full Rebuild (every 24h):**
   - Phase 1: Aggregates `single_type_info` docs grouped by endpoint (`url`, `method`, `apiCollectionId`) with `$min(timestamp)` for `discoveredTimestamp` and `$max(timestamp)` for `lastSeen` → `$out` to temp collection
   - Phase 2: Creates unique merge index on temp
   - Phase 3: `api_info` → `$merge` into temp with `whenNotMatched: "discard"` (STI endpoints are the source of truth, api_info only enriches)
   - Phase 4: Atomic `renameCollection` swap temp → live

2. **Incremental sync (between full rebuilds):**
   - Processes only STIs newer than last sync timestamp
   - Merges into live view with `$setUnion` for sensitive types
   - Refreshes api_info data via temp + swap

3. **Distributed lock** — `tryAcquire` uses atomic `findOneAndUpdate` with threshold-based CAS (30min for active accounts, 24h for inactive)

### Key design decisions

- **STI as source of truth** — The view contains all STI endpoints, not just the intersection of STI ∩ api_info. This means the total API count reflects all discovered endpoints, not just those with api_info entries.
- **`$ifNull` for api_info merge fields** — When merging api_info data, fields like `riskScore`, `severityScore`, `discoveredTimestamp`, `lastSeen` use `$ifNull($$new.field, $existing.field)` to avoid overwriting STI-derived values with null when api_info lacks those fields. `actualAuthType` and `actualAccessType` are always overwritten since they come exclusively from api_info.
- **`discoveredTimestamp` from STI** — Computed as `$min(timestamp)` from STI group, solving the issue where 42% of api_info docs were missing `discoveredTimestamp` (causing incorrect total API counts on the dashboard).
- **Deterministic auth type classification** — Uses `$filter` to keep only standard auth types from the `actualAuthType` array, with explicit UNAUTHENTICATED priority check. Avoids `$setUnion` non-deterministic ordering bug that caused auth type misclassification.
- **"Need more data" counts** — `countMissingFields` queries the view for endpoints with empty `actualAuthType`, `actualAccessType`, or null `apiType` to populate dashboard "Need more data" sections.
- **Temp collection + atomic rename** — Crash-safe, no stale data, no partial reads during rebuild
- **RBAC-aware queries** — View queries apply `UsersCollectionsList.getCollectionsIdForUser` filter
- **Feature-flagged** — Gated behind `AccountSettings.enableEndpointInfoView`, cron skips accounts without the flag

### Pre-computed fields in the view

| Field | Source | Computation |
|-------|--------|-------------|
| `discoveredTimestamp` | STI | `$min(timestamp)` per endpoint group |
| `lastSeen` | STI | `$max(timestamp)` per endpoint group |
| `sensitiveSubTypes` | STI | `$addToSet` of matching sensitive subtypes |
| `paramCount` | STI | `$sum(1)` count of params per endpoint |
| `actualAuthType` | api_info | `$reduce` + `$setUnion` to flatten `allAuthTypesFound` |
| `actualAccessType` | api_info | `apiAccessTypes` with null-safe default |
| `severity` | api_info | Buckets `severityScore` into CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW |
| `riskScore`, `severityScore`, `lastTested` | api_info | Direct fields with `$ifNull` fallback |
| `isOutOfTestingScope` | api_collections | Pre-computed from collection scope settings |
| `isHostCollection`, `hasHostHeader` | api_collections + STI | Host detection flags |

### Bug fixes in this PR

1. **`discoveredTimestamp` missing on 42% of docs** — Now computed from `$min(STI.timestamp)` instead of relying on api_info (which had 76% missing). Fixes dashboard showing only ~220k total APIs instead of full count.
2. **Auth type non-deterministic classification** — `$setUnion` produces non-deterministic array ordering, causing the first-element pick to randomly classify endpoints. Fixed by using `$filter` to keep only standard types + explicit UNAUTHENTICATED check.
3. **"Need more data" showing 0** — Was returning hardcoded zeros. Now queries actual missing field counts from the view via `countMissingFields`.

## Files changed

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `EndpointInfoViewCron.java` | Cron: STI group (full + incremental), api_info merge with `$ifNull`, flag check, 10min interval |
| `EndpointInfoViewDao.java` | Facet query with `$filter`-based auth type classification, `countMissingFields` for "Need more data" |
| `EndpointInfoViewTempDao.java` | Temp collection DAO with index creation + rename |
| `EndpointInfoView.java` | DTO with all pre-computed fields |
| `DashboardAction.java` | `fetchAPIInfosForMissingData` — returns actual missing counts from view |
| `ApiCollectionsAction.java` | `fetchApiStats` — view-first with fallback |
| `InventoryAction.java` | `fetchEndpointsCount` — view-first with fallback |
| `Account.java` | `stiLastFullRebuildTs`, `stiLastIncrementalTs`, `viewRefreshInitiateTs` |
| `AccountSettings.java` / `AccountSettingsDao.java` | `enableEndpointInfoView` feature flag |
| `MCollection.java` | `renameCollection` with `dropTarget(true)` |
| `DaoInit.java` | Register view index creation |
| `InitializerListener.java` | Schedule the cron |

title: new merging algo
body:
## Summary

Replaces the O(n²) brute-force URL merging algorithm with an optimized O(n·k) approach for the priority account (`1736798101`), gated behind `USE_OPTIMIZED_MERGING` env flag.

### New merging algorithm

- **Template-to-static matching**: Indexed lookup using a secondary wildcard-position index instead of generating all C(n,2) candidate keys per static URL. Only probes wildcard positions that actually exist in DB templates — fixes OOM on long URLs.
- **Static-to-static matching** (`OptimizedMerger`): Two-tier signature-based grouping:
  - **Tier 1**: Free-merge tokens (INT/UUID/VER/LOC) are tagged in a signature key — URLs with identical signatures merge instantly.
  - **Tier 2**: For remaining singletons, skip one ALNUM position to discover new templates (handles exactly-one string diff).
- **Over-broad template skip**: Templates where all tokens are wildcards (e.g. `STRING/STRING`) are excluded from the index.
- **Deduplication**: Handles duplicate template entries with/without leading `/`.
- **`api` token guard**: Prevents `api` from being classified as OPAQUE (avoids false merges like `/api/v4/STRING`).

### Audit mode (dry-run)

For the optimized account, merging writes results to `merge_audit_logs` collection instead of performing deletions:
- Each doc records: `apiCollectionId`, `mergeType` (TEMPLATE_TO_STATIC / STATIC_TO_STATIC), `templateUrl`, `method`, `matchedStaticUrls`, `discoveredAt`
- Subsequent runs skip already-audited static URLs via `MergeAuditLogDao.getAuditedStaticUrls()`
- `Cron.verifyAuditLogs()` prints verification stats (unique URLs to delete, per-collection counts, ApiInfo/STI impact, multi-template conflicts)

### Deletion cron

Behind `ENABLE_MERGE_AUDIT_DELETION` env flag (runs only for priority account):
- Reads `merge_audit_logs` docs where deletion is incomplete
- Groups static URLs by `(apiCollectionId, method)` for efficient `$in` batch deletes
- Deletes from STI, ApiInfo, SampleData independently — tracks success per entity type
- Marks `stiDeleted`, `apiInfoDeleted`, `sampleDataDeleted` booleans via single bulk `updateMany` per batch
- If one entity type fails, only that boolean stays unmarked for retry on next run

### Files changed

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `OptimizedMerger.java` | New — Tier 1/Tier 2 static-to-static merging |
| `MergingLogic.java` | Refactored template index with wildcard position tracking, audit log save/load, leading `/` normalization |
| `MergeAuditDeletion.java` | New — batch deletion cron logic |
| `Cron.java` | Deletion cron wiring, `verifyAuditLogs()` |
| `MergeAuditLog.java` | New DTO with 3 deletion-tracking booleans |
| `MergeAuditLogDao.java` | New DAO with `getAuditedStaticUrls()` |
| `TestOptimizedMerger.java` | Unit tests for token classification, signatures, tier 1/2 merging |
| `TestOptimizedTemplateToStaticMatch.java` | Updated tests for refactored template index |

## Test plan

- [x] `TestOptimizedMerger` — token classification, tier 1/tier 2 signatures, end-to-end merge correctness
- [x] `TestOptimizedTemplateToStaticMatch` — indexed template-to-static matching
- [ ] Run on priority account with `USE_OPTIMIZED_MERGING=true` in audit mode, verify `merge_audit_logs` via `verifyAuditLogs()`
- [ ] Enable `ENABLE_MERGE_AUDIT_DELETION=true`, verify STI/ApiInfo/SampleData deletions and boolean tracking
- [ ] Verify old merging flow unaffected for non-optimized accounts

body:
## API Hit Count

Tracks how many times each API endpoint is called per minute across all consumers to detect API-level abuse (e.g. a flood of requests to one endpoint across many IPs, each individually under the per-IP rate limit).

### How it works

**Hot path**: Per request, two extra fields (`apiLevelWindow`, `apiLevelThreshold`) are packed into the existing `threat_input_stream` Redis stream message. Config is fetched from `FilterCache.getApiLevelRateLimitRule()` and embedded in the message so the background consumer needs no access to filter state.

**Cold path (Lua)**: The existing `async_threat_process.lua` script handles API hit counting alongside IP distribution:
- `INCR apiCount|{collectionId}|{url}|{method}|{binId}` per request (8h TTL)
- `ZADD apiCountIndex score={binId}` to index active APIs for the relay cron
- Sliding window sum across `apiLevelWindow` bins — if total ≥ `apiLevelThreshold`, returns a breach to Java which pushes a `MaliciousEventKafkaEnvelope` alert

**Relay cron (every 1 min)**: Reads all per-bin counts from Redis via `ZRANGEBYSCORE` + `MGET` and bulk-inserts `ApiHitCountInfo` records to DB for dashboards.

---

## Bug Fix: Negative Bucket Counts in IP/API Distribution

### Root cause

The distribution module buckets unique IP+API pairs by request count (b1=1–10, b2=11–50, etc.) using a Count-Min Sketch (CMS). The original logic detected "first time this IP+API is seen in this window" by checking `if count == 1` after querying the CMS.

**CMS is probabilistic and can overestimate.** The error bound is `epsilon × N` where N is total insertions across all keys in the sketch for that minute. With `epsilon=0.01` and just 100 unique IP+API pairs per minute, the overestimate is already ≥ 1 — meaning a new IP+API's very first request returns `count=2` instead of `1`. The `count==1` guard is skipped, `b1` never gets its initial `+1`, but at the b1→b2 boundary (count=11) `b1` gets decremented → **b1 goes negative**.

Confirmed via Redis logs: every first-seen overestimate shows `count=2`, and every negative guard trigger shows `count=11` (the b1→b2 boundary), `val=0` (b1 was never incremented).

### Fix

Replaced the fragile `count==1` / `getBucketLabel(count-1)` inference with a `prevBuckets|{windowSize}|{windowStart}` Redis hash that stores the last known bucket per IP+API pair per window.

```lua
local prevBucket = redis.call('HGET', prevBucketHashKey, ipApiCmsKey)

if prevBucket == false then
    -- first time this IP+API seen in this window
    redis.call('HINCRBY', distKey, newBucket, 1)
elseif prevBucket ~= newBucket then
    redis.call('HINCRBY', distKey, prevBucket, -1)
    redis.call('HINCRBY', distKey, newBucket, 1)
end

redis.call('HSET', prevBucketHashKey, ipApiCmsKey, newBucket)
```

- First-seen detection is now via `HGET` returning `false` (nil) — independent of CMS accuracy
- Transitions always use the actual last stored bucket, not `count-1` arithmetic
- Negative counts are now impossible regardless of CMS overestimation or pod concurrency
- `HGET`+`HSET` within the same atomic Lua script — no race conditions across pods

feat: classify HTTP traffic headers (user-agent, referer) into API tags
body:
## Summary

Classifies \`user-agent\` and \`referer\` headers from Kafka traffic into named categories and stores them as \`tagsList\` on \`ApiInfo\` in MongoDB. Each API endpoint accumulates tags as traffic flows through it — enabling traffic source analysis (browser vs bot vs infra vs AI agent, etc).

## Flow

\`\`\`
Kafka message
  └─► SampleParser.parse()
        └─► HttpResponseParams
              └─► Main.handleResponseParams()
                    └─► HttpCallParser.syncFunction()
                          ├─► AktoPolicyNew.process()  ← per message
                          │     ├─► UserAgentClassifier.classify(ua)
                          │     │     └─► INFRA → BOT → AI_AGENT → MOBILE_APP
                          │     │               → BROWSER → API_CLIENT → UNKNOWN
                          │     ├─► UserAgentClassifier.extractRefererHost(referer)
                          │     └─► addClassifiedTag(apiInfo, keyName, value)
                          │           ├─► update value if keyName already exists
                          │           └─► append new entry if keyName is new
                          └─► APICatalogSync.syncWithDB()  ← periodic batch
                                └─► ApiInfoBulkUpdate.getUpdatesForApiInfo()
                                      └─► $set tagsList atomically
\`\`\`

## User-Agent Classification Priority

| Priority | Category | Example UAs |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | INFRA | kube-probe, prometheus, datadog, envoy |
| 2 | BOT | Googlebot, Bingbot, AhrefsBot, crawler |
| 3 | AI_AGENT | langchain, openai-python, litellm, crewai |
| 4 | MOBILE_APP | okhttp, CFNetwork, flutter, android, dart |
| 5 | BROWSER | Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge, Chromium |
| 6 | API_CLIENT | curl, python-requests, axios, grpc, postman |
| 7 | UNKNOWN | anything that matches no rule |

First match wins. Regex patterns are compiled once at class load (static block).

## Merge Behaviour for tagsList

- **Same \`keyName\` exists** → update \`value\` + \`lastUpdatedTs\`
- **New \`keyName\`** → append to list
- **DB write** uses \`$set\` on entire array — required because \`CollectionTags\` are objects; \`$addEachToSet\` cannot deduplicate by \`keyName\` alone
- **\`ApiInfo.merge()\`** deduplicates by \`keyName\` + \`value\` pair when merging in-memory catalogs

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| \`UserAgentClassifier.java\` | **New** — regex-based priority classifier returning \`Category\` enum; \`extractRefererHost()\` parses hostname from referer URL |
| \`AktoPolicyNew.java\` | Extracts UA + referer per request, classifies, calls \`addClassifiedTag()\` to update \`ApiInfo.tagsList\` in memory |
| \`ApiInfo.java\` | Added \`tagsList: List<CollectionTags>\` field, constant, getter/setter, merge logic |
| \`ApiInfoBulkUpdate.java\` | Writes \`tagsList\` via \`$set\` (both mini-runtime and cyborg paths) |
| \`KafkaProducerExample.java\` | Added \`referer-test\` mode and updated \`load\` mode with 10k unique hosts, 20 paths, 5 methods, randomised UA + referer |

title: Feature/optimise template static url matching
body:
## Summary

Optimizes URL merging for large collections (1M+ STIs) that were causing the merging cron to get stuck.

### Changes

**Optimized template-to-static matching (`MergingLogic.java`)**
- Replaces O(m×n) brute-force template-to-static matching with O(1) indexed lookup using `(method, tokenCount, fixedTokenPositions)` keys
- For each static URL, generates candidate keys by skipping 0/1/2 wildcard positions — hashmap lookup instead of iterating all templates
- Key generation uses direct `buildKeyDirect()` with skip indices — no intermediate HashMap/sorting allocations

**Collection-level skip for optimized account (`Cron.java`)**
- When `USE_OPTIMIZED_MERGING=true`, skips merging entirely for non-flagged collections in the target account
- Only flagged collections (configured via `OPTIMIZED_MERGING_COLLECTION_IDS` env var) get the optimized merging path
- Other accounts are completely unaffected

**Optimized merging path for flagged collections**
- Fetches only host-header STIs (not all body param STIs) — dramatically reduces data fetched from DB
- Uses indexed template-to-static matching instead of O(n²) static-to-static
- Skips static-to-static matching entirely (safe direction: may under-merge but never over-merge)

**Test coverage (`TestOptimizedTemplateToStaticMatch.java`)**
- ~40 JUnit tests comparing optimized vs brute-force results across all edge cases
- Covers: basic types (INTEGER/STRING), multiple wildcards, method mismatches, URL normalization, invalid inputs, scale tests (500 templates × 5000 statics), ordering independence, English word rejection, unrecognized types (OBJECT_ID/FLOAT/UUID treated as literals)

### Example: How indexed lookup works

**Templates in DB:**
```
GET /api/users/INTEGER        → tokens: ["api", "users", null], types: [-, -, INTEGER]
GET /api/orders/INTEGER/details → tokens: ["api", "orders", null, "details"], types: [-, -, INTEGER, -]
```

**Indexing step** — each template is keyed by its fixed token positions:
```
"GET|3|0:api|1:users"             → [GET /api/users/INTEGER]
"GET|4|0:api|1:orders|3:details"  → [GET /api/orders/INTEGER/details]
```

**Matching static URL** `GET /api/users/42`:
1. Tokens: `["api", "users", "42"]`, method=GET, tokenCount=3
2. Generate candidate keys by skipping 0, 1, or 2 positions:
   - Skip none: `"GET|3|0:api|1:users|2:42"` → no match in index
   - Skip pos 0: `"GET|3|1:users|2:42"` → no match
   - Skip pos 1: `"GET|3|0:api|2:42"` → no match
   - **Skip pos 2**: `"GET|3|0:api|1:users"` → **HIT!** → found template `GET /api/users/INTEGER`
3. Verify via `URLTemplate.match("api/users/42", GET)` → `42` is a valid INTEGER → **matched**

**Result:** Instead of checking all m templates for each static URL (O(m×n)), we do at most `1 + n + n*(n-1)/2` hashmap lookups per static URL (bounded by `MAX_WILDCARD_POSITIONS=2`), which is O(1) per URL for typical APIs with ≤10 tokens.

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `USE_OPTIMIZED_MERGING` | `false` | Enable optimized merging + collection skipping for the target account |
| `OPTIMIZED_MERGING_COLLECTION_IDS` | empty | Comma-separated collection IDs to apply optimized merging (e.g. `503341241,-1917146520`) |

### Safety

- **No over-merging risk**: Optimization only affects template-to-static matching (not template discovery). Worst case is under-merging if `MAX_WILDCARD_POSITIONS=2` misses templates with 3+ wildcards.
- **Gated to specific account**: Only account `1736798101` is affected when enabled. All other accounts use the original unchanged path.
- **Kill switch**: Set `USE_OPTIMIZED_MERGING=false` (or unset) to revert to old behavior completely.

Add THREAT_DETECTION rolling reboot cron
body:
## Summary

- Ports `ModuleInfo`, `ModuleInfoDao`, `ModuleInfoConstants`, `ModuleInfoAction`, and `struts.xml` entries from master to support the cron's dependencies
- Adds `setUpThreatDetectionRollingRebootScheduler` in `InitializerListener`, scoped to account `1758787662`

## Cron Flow

```
Every 2 hours (+ random jitter up to 5 min)
│
└── AccountTask.executeTask (all accounts)
    │
    ├── account.getId() != 1758787662 → return (skip)
    │
    └── account 1758787662
        │
        ├── ModuleInfoDao.fetchLiveModulesByType(THREAT_DETECTION)
        │     └── filter: moduleType=THREAT_DETECTION
        │                 lastHeartbeatReceived >= now - 5min
        │
        ├── liveModules is empty → log & return
        │
        └── for each module (one by one):
              │
              ├── ModuleInfoDao.triggerReboot(moduleId, THREAT_DETECTION)
              │     └── filter: id=moduleId
              │                 lastHeartbeatReceived >= now - 2min
              │                 moduleType=THREAT_DETECTION
              │     └── update: reboot = true
              │
              └── (if not last module)
                    sleep random 60–180 seconds
                    → repeat for next module
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify cron does not execute for accounts other than `1758787662`
- [ ] Verify only modules with heartbeat within 5 min are fetched
- [ ] Verify reboot flag is set only if module has heartbeat within 2 min at reboot time
- [ ] Verify multiple modules are rebooted sequentially with a gap, not in parallel

- Add `LLMService.callLLM()` as shared LLM invocation utility used by both `LLMAction` and `SkillValidationAction` — eliminates duplication of Azure OpenAI / AgentModelDao logic
- Add `SkillValidationAction`: new Struts endpoint `api/validateAndReportSkill` that validates agent skill file content via LLM, writes audit log to `mcp_audit_info`, and fires threat report to `tbs.akto.io` if flagged

Feature/sequence anomally detection
body:
## Summary

Implements sequence-based anomaly detection on top of the API sequence probability model built by mini-runtime.

## Flow

```
mini-runtime (feature/mini-runtime-release)
    → SessionAnalyzer: per-user deque tracks API call sequences
    → WindowAccumulator: counts transitions (A→B) per 10-min tumbling window
    → ApiSequencesFlusher: upserts to MongoDB api_sequences collection
        { paths: ["/login#POST", "/dashboard#GET"], probability: 0.82, ... }

threat-detection (this branch)
    → SequenceCache (new): loads api_sequences from MongoDB every 10 min
        Map<"prevApi|currentApi", probability>

    Per request in MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask.processRecord():
        1. actor = sourceIP (Kafka-partitioned — each IP always hits same instance)
        2. urlForAggregation = templatized URL (e.g. /users/INTEGER)
        3. currentApiKey = "{collectionId} {url} {method}"
        4. checkSequenceAnomaly(actor, currentApiKey)  ← new, in-memory only
              prevApiKey = actorLastApi.get(actor)      ← Caffeine, TTL 10 min
              actorLastApi.put(actor, currentApiKey)
              if prevApiKey == null: skip (first request)
              probability = sequenceCache.get(prevApiKey|currentApiKey)
              if probability == null OR probability < 0.05: anomalous
                  actorAnomalyCount[actor]++
                  if count >= 5:
                      actorAnomalyCount.invalidate(actor)
                      → generateAndPushMaliciousEventRequest(SequenceAnomaly, SINGLE)
                            → internalKafka → KafkaTopic.ThreatDetection.ALERTS
                                → SendMaliciousEventsToBackend → dashboard
```

**Key design decisions:**
- No Redis on the hot path — all state is Caffeine in-memory
- No reset on normal transitions — counter accumulates across the window, only resets after alert or TTL expiry (prevents bypass by mixing normal requests)
- Kafka partitioned by source IP → single instance owns all requests per actor, no cross-instance state sharing needed
- `SequenceCache` owns all detection state (probabilities + per-actor tracking) — independently testable without constructing the full task

## Changes

- **`libs/dao`**: `ApiSequences` DTO/DAO sync with `feature/mini-runtime-release` — removed `@BsonId int id`, added `lastStateCount`, unique compound index on `(apiCollectionId, paths)`
- **`libs/utils`**: `DataActor` / `DbActor` / `DbLayer` / `ClientActor` — added `fetchApiSequences()`
- **`apps/threat-detection`**:
  - `SequenceCache` — transition probability cache + per-actor anomaly tracking
  - `Utils.buildSequenceAnomalyFilter()` — synthetic `FilterConfig` (category=Behavioral, severity=HIGH)
  - `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask` — wires `SequenceCache`, delegates to `checkSequenceAnomaly()`
  - `SequenceCacheTest` — 11 behavioral tests covering threshold, counter accumulation, actor isolation, boundary conditions

## Related PRs
- database-abstractor `fetchApiSequences` endpoint: akto-api-security/akto#5004 (against `feature/cyborg-release`)

## Summary

This PR refactors the `threat-detection` module focusing on `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask` and the Kafka configuration layer. No behavioural changes — pure structural cleanup.

### Kafka config (`libs/utils`)
- Added `fetchMaxBytes` field to `KafkaConsumerConfig` so consumers can declare their fetch size in config rather than hardcoding it in `Properties` setup
- Added `toConsumerProperties()` to `KafkaConfig` — single place that translates the typed config object into the `Properties` map the Kafka client requires
- Fixed a pre-existing bug in `AbstractKafkaConsumerTask`: key deserializer was incorrectly set to the value serializer

### `AbstractKafkaConsumerTask`
- Consumer construction now uses `kafkaConfig.toConsumerProperties()` — no more duplicate `Properties` setup in subclasses
- Added `beforePollLoop()` hook for subclasses to run setup before polling starts
- Removed `if (records.isEmpty()) continue` guard — was preventing metrics logging during low-traffic periods in `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask`

### `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask`
- Now extends `AbstractKafkaConsumerTask<byte[]>` — eliminates duplicate Kafka consumer setup and the polling loop boilerplate
- Removed `kafkaPollingEnabled` static boolean (read once at startup, always true, not a real kill switch)
- Extracted `FilterCache` class (`cache/`) — owns filter state (`apiFilters`, `successfulExploitFilters`, `ignoredEventFilters`), TTL-based refresh, and OpenAPI schema Redis cache. Fixes a bug where `successfulExploitFilters` and `ignoredEventFilters` were `static` mutable lists
- Moved `handleSchemaConformFilter` to `RequestValidator` where the rest of schema validation logic lives
- Moved `getRedactionType` + `extractHostFromHeaders` to `Utils` — stateless helpers reusable by other components (e.g. `HyperscanEventHandler`)
- Removed unused `trackAndLogValidHostname` + `isValidHostname` methods and their associated dead state fields
- Extracted per-minute metrics logging into `logRecordsPerMin(int count)`
- Topic name `"akto.api.logs2"` moved to `KafkaTopic.TRAFFIC_LOGS` constant
- Removed all inline `java.util.*` imports, standardised at top

### Other
- Removed `CLAUDE.md` from `.gitignore` — the file contains module architecture docs useful to all contributors
- `Main.java` traffic Kafka config now explicitly sets `fetchMaxBytes = 100MB` (was hardcoded inside `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask` constructor previously)

## Review notes
- `buildHttpResponseParam` intentionally stays in `MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask` — it reuses static `requestParams`/`responseParams` objects for performance on the hot Kafka path (single-threaded by design, documented in CLAUDE.md)
- `FilterCache.getApiSchema` handles `null` Redis connection gracefully — falls back to direct DB fetch when Redis is unavailable
- Schema conformance detection (`SchemaConform` category) remains gated to specific account IDs and is unchanged

- [ ] Verify filters are fetched and bucketed correctly on first poll and after TTL expiry
- [ ] Verify `fetchMaxBytes` is applied for the traffic consumer (check consumer config logs at startup)
- [ ] Verify threat detection events are still published correctly for both YAML filter and Hyperscan paths

title: [DON"T MERGE]Feature/variable markov sequence
body:
## Summary

Implements Variable Order Markov Chains (VOMC) for API sequence learning, extending the fixed-length pair (A→B) model to adaptive multi-order sequences (up to order 10). Higher-order contexts are automatically pruned when they don't carry statistically distinct information, producing a compact behavioral model.

---

## How It Works

### Per-Record Hot Path (Multi-Order Emission)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[HttpResponseParams arrives] --> B[AktoPolicyNew.generateFromHttpResponseParams\nRaw URL → templatized ApiInfoKey]
    B --> C{ApiInfoKey known in\napiInfoCatalogMap?}
    C -- No --> X[Skip record]
    C -- Yes --> D[IpBasedIdentifier.extractUserId\nIP address as user identity]
    D --> E[Get/create UserSessionState\nper-user deque of last maxOrder APIs]
    E --> F{Deque stale?\nsessionStart < windowStart}
    F -- Yes --> G[Reset deque + sessionStart]
    F -- No --> H
    G --> H[Multi-order emission loop]

    H --> I["for order = 1 to maxOrder:"]
    I --> J{deque.size >= order?}
    J -- Yes --> K["Build TransitionKey\ntake last 'order' items from deque + current API\ne.g. order=2, deque=[A,B,C]: → [B,C,current]"]
    K --> L[accumulator.recordTransition\nConcurrentHashMap + LongAdder]
    J -- No --> M[Skip this order]
    L --> I
    M --> I

    I --> N[accumulator.recordApiCall]
    N --> O["Update deque: addLast(apiKey)\nif size > maxOrder: removeFirst"]
```

### Example: maxOrder=3, User calls A → B → C → D

```
Call A: deque=[]
  → No transitions (deque empty for all orders)
  → deque=[A]

Call B: deque=[A]
  → Order 1: [A → B]           (deque has ≥1 item)
  → Order 2: skip              (deque has <2 items)
  → Order 3: skip              (deque has <3 items)
  → deque=[A, B]

Call C: deque=[A, B]
  → Order 1: [B → C]           (last 1 + current)
  → Order 2: [A → B → C]       (last 2 + current)
  → Order 3: skip              (deque has <3 items)
  → deque=[A, B, C]

Call D: deque=[A, B, C]
  → Order 1: [C → D]           (last 1 + current)
  → Order 2: [B → C → D]       (last 2 + current)
  → Order 3: [A → B → C → D]   (last 3 + current)
  → deque=[B, C, D]            (A dropped, max size = 3)

Total: 6 transitions across 3 orders
```

### Window Flip + VOMC Pruning + Flush

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant K as Kafka records
    participant SA as SessionAnalyzer
    participant CA as CurrentAccumulator
    participant NA as NewAccumulator
    participant MB as MarkovModelBuilder
    participant F as ApiSequencesFlusher
    participant DB as MongoDB

    K->>SA: process() calls stream in
    Note over SA,CA: All orders 1..maxOrder accumulate into single window

    Note over SA: Window end (every 10 min)
    SA->>NA: Create fresh accumulator
    SA-->>CA: volatile swap: currentAccumulator = NA
    SA->>CA: snapshot(windowStart, windowEnd)

    SA->>F: CompletableFuture.runAsync → flush(snapshot)

    F->>MB: MarkovModelBuilder.prune(transitionCounts)
    Note over MB: VOMC collapsibility algorithm:\n1. Group transitions by context\n2. For each order N (highest first):\n   compute credible intervals (Beta dist)\n3. If ALL intervals overlap with parent → collapse\n4. If ANY interval differs → keep

    MB-->>F: pruned transition map

    F->>F: Build ApiSequences list\nFor each surviving transition:\n  paths, transitionCount, prevStateCount,\n  lastStateCount
    F->>F: Sort by transitionCount desc\nKeep top 1000 only

    F->>DB: DataActor.writeApiSequences()
    Note over DB: Aggregation pipeline upsert:\nStage 1: $add counts + $ifNull for createdAt/isActive\nStage 2: $divide for probability + precedenceScore
```

### VOMC Collapsibility — When to Prune

**Collapsible (gets pruned):** 100 users all do `login → dashboard → settings`

```
Order-1 context [dashboard]:     → settings 100%
Order-2 context [login,dashboard]: → settings 100%    ← SAME distribution → COLLAPSE
```
Credible intervals overlap completely → order-2 context is redundant.

**Non-collapsible (survives):** 50 users do `login → dashboard → settings`, 50 do `admin → dashboard → admin`

```
Order-1 context [dashboard]:       → settings 50%, admin 50%
Order-2 context [login,dashboard]: → settings 100%    ← DIFFERENT → KEEP
Order-2 context [admin,dashboard]: → admin 100%       ← DIFFERENT → KEEP
```
Credible intervals don't overlap → order-2 contexts carry distinct information.

### MongoDB Document Shape

Each flushed sequence becomes an upsert keyed on `(apiCollectionId, paths)`:

```json
{
  "apiCollectionId": 1738051798,
  "paths": ["1738051798 GET /accounts", "1738051798 GET /accounts/STRING/transactions"],
  "transitionCount": 830,
  "prevStateCount": 1820,
  "lastStateCount": 943,
  "probability": 0.456,
  "precedenceScore": 0.880,
  "lastUpdatedAt": 1714300000,
  "createdAt": 1714200000,
  "isActive": true
}
```

- `probability = transitionCount / prevStateCount` (computed in DB via `$divide`)
- `precedenceScore = transitionCount / lastStateCount` (how reliably the last endpoint is preceded by this sequence)
- `paths.size() - 1` = the Markov order (no separate field needed)

---

## Module Structure

```
behaviour_modelling/
├── core/
│   ├── UserIdentifier.java         — extracts user identity from HttpResponseParams
│   ├── WindowAccumulator.java      — accumulates counts; userId param for phase-2 weighting
│   ├── WindowFlusher.java          — receives WindowSnapshot at end of each window
│   └── MarkovModelBuilder.java     — VOMC collapsibility: prunes redundant higher-order contexts
├── model/
│   ├── TransitionKey.java          — ApiInfoKey[] n-gram (variable length = variable order)
│   ├── UserSessionState.java       — per-user Deque<ApiInfoKey> of size maxOrder
│   └── WindowSnapshot.java         — immutable Map<ApiInfoKey,Long> + Map<TransitionKey,Long>
├── impl/
│   ├── IpBasedIdentifier.java      — uses sourceIP as user identity
│   ├── RawCountAccumulator.java    — ConcurrentHashMap<LongAdder> for all orders
│   └── ApiSequencesFlusher.java    — VOMC prune → top-1000 cap → DataActor.writeApiSequences()
├── SequenceAnalyzerConfig.java     — maxOrder (10), windowDurationMs, factories
└── SessionAnalyzer.java            — orchestrator: multi-order emission, atomic window flip
```

---

## Test Plan

- [x] Test A: Multi-order emission — 4-API sequence with maxOrder=3, verify 6 transitions across 3 orders
- [x] Test B: VOMC collapsible — uniform pattern, order-2 contexts collapse into order-1
- [x] Test C: VOMC non-collapsible — divergent patterns, order-2 contexts survive pruning
- [x] Test D: Precedence score e2e — verify transitionCount/prevStateCount/lastStateCount structure
- [x] Test E: Top-1000 cap — 1099 unique transitions, verify snapshot integrity
- [x] Test F: Window boundary with maxOrder=3 — deque reset prevents cross-window transitions

title: Rate limit optimisations scram
body:
## Summary

Optimises rate-limit detection in `threat-detection` by moving **all Redis operations off the Kafka hot path** — replacing synchronous `EVALSHA` calls (which halved throughput from ~5500 to ~2500 msg/sec) with a fully async Redis Stream pipeline.

### Key Changes

- **Zero sync Redis calls on hot path**: Kafka consumer now only does an async `XADD` to a Redis Stream per message
- **Batch Lua processing**: A background stream consumer batches up to 500 messages and processes them in a single `EVALSHA` call — amortising network round trips
- **CMS moved to Redis (RedisBloom)**: Replaced in-memory `CountMinSketch` with `CMS.INITBYPROB` / `CMS.INCRBY` / `CMS.QUERY` in Redis — centralised, no cross-pod sync needed
- **Distribution race condition fixed**: CMS increment + distribution bucket update now happen atomically in the same Lua script — eliminates negative bucket counts
- **Mitigation check in Lua**: `isActorInMitigationPeriod` moved into the Lua script to avoid extra sync Redis calls
- **Bucket boundary fix**: Changed `count < max` to `count <= max` in Lua to match inclusive bucket ranges from `ThreatApiDistributionUtils`

## Architecture Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        KAFKA CONSUMER                           │
│                   (MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask)                │
│                                                                 │
│  For each message:                                              │
│    1. Parse HttpResponseParams                                  │
│    2. Run filter matching (malicious traffic detection)         │
│    3. If apiDistributionEnabled:                                │
│       └─ async XADD to "threat_input_stream"                   │
│          (ipApiCmsKey, apiKey, epochMin, threshold,             │
│           host, accountId, rateLimitWindow)                     │
│                                                                 │
│  ⚡ Zero sync Redis calls = full ~5500 msg/sec throughput       │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ async XADD
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    REDIS STREAM                                  │
│               "threat_input_stream"                              │
│                                                                 │
│  Messages accumulate here. Consumer group "threat_group"         │
│  ensures each message is processed exactly once.                │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ XREADGROUP (batch up to 500)
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                STREAM CONSUMER (Background Thread)              │
│                  (DistributionStreamConsumer)                    │
│                                                                 │
│  1. XREADGROUP COUNT 500 from "threat_input_stream"             │
│  2. Group messages into batch                                   │
│  3. Single EVALSHA call with entire batch                       │
│     └─ 500 messages × 1 round trip = 500x fewer round trips    │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ EVALSHA
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              LUA SCRIPT (async_threat_process.lua)               │
│              Runs atomically in Redis (single-threaded)          │
│                                                                 │
│  For each message in batch:                                     │
│    1. CMS.INITBYPROB (if key doesn't exist)                    │
│    2. CMS.INCRBY → increment count for IP+API in current min   │
│    3. EXPIRE on CMS key (8hr TTL)                               │
│    4. CMS.QUERY across sliding window → slidingCount            │
│    5. Distribution update:                                      │
│       ├─ getBucketLabel(count) → newBucket                      │
│       ├─ getBucketLabel(count-1) → oldBucket                    │
│       ├─ If count == 1: HINCRBY dist newBucket +1               │
│       └─ If oldBucket ≠ newBucket: HINCRBY old -1, new +1      │
│    6. SADD to active APIs set                                   │
│    7. Threshold check:                                          │
│       ├─ EXISTS mitigation key → skip if in cooldown            │
│       ├─ If slidingCount > threshold:                           │
│       │   └─ SETEX mitigation key (5 min TTL)                  │
│       │   └─ Add to breaches list                               │
│       └─ Return breaches to Java                                │
│                                                                 │
│  ✅ CMS + Distribution atomic = no race condition               │
│  ✅ No negative bucket counts                                   │
└──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┘
                           │ breaches returned
                           ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            BREACH EVENT HANDLER (in StreamConsumer)              │
│                                                                 │
│  For each breach:                                               │
│    1. Parse ipApiCmsKey → IP, apiCollectionId, url, method      │
│    2. Build MaliciousEventMessage (from stream message fields)  │
│    3. Push to internal Kafka topic                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Redis Data Model

```
cms|{epochMin}                          → RedisBloom CMS sketch (8hr TTL)
dist|{windowSize}|{windowStart}|{api}   → Hash {b1: count, b2: count, ...}
distApis|{windowSize}|{windowStart}     → Set of active API keys
mitigate|{ipApiCmsKey}                  → String "1" (5 min TTL)
threat_input_stream                     → Redis Stream (consumer group: threat_group)
```

### Multi-Pod Behaviour
- All pods share the same Redis instance
- Kafka is IP-partitioned → same IP always routes to same pod
- Each pod runs 1 stream consumer with a unique consumer ID (instanceId)
- Consumer group ensures each stream message is processed exactly once
- CMS operations are commutative (order-independent) — safe across pods

### Files Changed
- **`async_threat_process.lua`** — New mega Lua script (CMS + distribution + mitigation + threshold)
- **`cms_increment_and_query.lua`** / **`cms_range_query.lua`** — Retained for `ParamEnumerationDetector`
- **`DistributionStreamConsumer.java`** — New stream consumer with batch EVALSHA
- **`DistributionCalculator.java`** — Simplified to async XADD only
- **`CmsCounterLayer.java`** — Rewritten to use Redis-backed CMS via Lua scripts
- **`MaliciousTrafficDetectorTask.java`** — Hot path no longer calls sync Redis
- **`CmsDataForwardLayer.java`** / **`distribution_update.lua`** — Deleted (obsolete)

- [x] Stream consumer: all messages consumed (lag=0, pending=0)

detect and change agg rule to false on new pod
body:
## Problem

When a new threat-detection pod spins up, its environment has `AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED=true` by default. The pod needs this set to `false` so it stops running aggregation rules and instead triggers an internal process restart — without a full pod restart.

## Flow

```
Pod starts up
     │
     ▼
Every 60s: heartbeat sent → updateModuleInfo() called
     │
     ├─► [First heartbeat] Doc doesn't exist yet
     │        │
     │        └─► findOneAndUpdate (upsert) creates doc with AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED="true"
     │
     └─► [Subsequent heartbeats] Doc exists
              │
              ▼
        updateModuleEnvAndReboot(moduleInfo)
              │
              ├─ Early return if additionalData/env missing
              ├─ Early return if AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED != "true" (in-memory check)
              │
              ▼
        DB update (only if DB value is still "true"):
          - SET additionalData.env.AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED = false
          - SET _reboot = true
          + mutate in-memory moduleInfo.env to "false"
              │
              ▼
        findOneAndUpdate persists additionalData with "false"
              │
              ▼
        Pod polls DB, sees _reboot=true → internal process restart
              │
              ▼
        Next heartbeat carries AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED="false"
        → early return, no more updates
```

## Why the DB filter matters

After the first DB write sets `AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED=false`, the pod continues sending heartbeats with `true` in its env (until it internally restarts, ~2 min). Without a DB-side filter, the update would fire on every heartbeat during this window.

The filter `Filters.eq("additionalData.env.AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED", "true")` makes subsequent writes a no-op once the DB value is already `false` — preventing redundant `_reboot=true` signals.

## Why the in-memory mutation matters

`updateModuleEnvAndReboot` runs before the main `findOneAndUpdate`. Without mutating the in-memory `moduleInfo` object, the main query would overwrite `additionalData` back to `true` (from the heartbeat payload), undoing the DB update.

## Changes

- `updateModuleEnvAndReboot()` — new method that detects `AGGREGATION_RULES_ENABLED=true` and sets it to `false` + triggers internal reboot signal
- Called only for account `1758787662` inside `updateModuleInfo()`
- DB filter prevents redundant writes during the ~2 min internal restart window
- In-memory mutation ensures the subsequent heartbeat upsert does not overwrite the change

title: feat: user session sequence analyzer for API behaviour modelling
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new \`behaviour_modelling\` module under \`mini-runtime\` that tracks per-user API call sequences within tumbling 10-minute windows
- Aggregates API call counts and transition counts (A→B pairs, extensible to N-grams) for downstream sequence probability modelling
- Uses \`AktoPolicyNew\` for URL templatization (raw URLs → parametrized templates like \`/users/INTEGER\`) without any extra DB calls
- Flushes per-window transition probabilities to MongoDB \`api_sequences\` via the \`DataActor\`/\`DbActor\`/\`ClientActor\` abstraction layer
- Designed for 50-100k req/min throughput with minimal memory footprint

---

## How It Works

### Per-record hot path

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[HttpResponseParams arrives] --> B[AktoPolicyNew.generateFromHttpResponseParams\nRaw URL → templatized ApiInfoKey]
    B --> C{ApiInfoKey known in\napiInfoCatalogMap?}
    C -- No, unknown API --> X[Skip record]
    C -- Yes --> D[UserIdentifier.extractUserId\nIP address for now]
    D --> E{UserSessionState\nexists?}
    E -- No --> F[Create new state\ndeque = empty\nsessionStart = now]
    E -- Yes --> G{sessionStart\n< windowStart?}
    F --> H
    G -- Yes, stale window --> I[Reset deque\nsessionStart = now]
    G -- No, same window --> H
    I --> H[Check deque size\nsequenceLength - 1 = 1]
    H -- deque has 1 entry --> J[Build TransitionKey\ndeque-0 → current ApiInfoKey\ne.g. GET:/orders → POST:/checkout]
    H -- deque empty --> K
    J --> K[WindowAccumulator\nrecordTransition + recordApiCall]
    K --> L[Push ApiInfoKey onto deque\npop front if size >= sequenceLength-1]
```

### 2-length sequence example (single user, one 10-min window)

```
t=0m  User calls  GET /products          deque: []          → no transition yet
                                          apiCounts: { GET:/products: 1 }

t=1m  User calls  GET /products/abc123   templatized → GET /products/STRING
      deque: [GET:/products]
                                          → emit transition  GET:/products → GET:/products/STRING
                                          apiCounts: { GET:/products: 1, GET:/products/STRING: 1 }
                                          transitionCounts: { GET:/products → GET:/products/STRING : 1 }

t=3m  User calls  POST /cart/add         deque: [GET:/products/STRING]
                                          → emit transition  GET:/products/STRING → POST:/cart/add
                                          apiCounts: { ..., POST:/cart/add: 1 }
                                          transitionCounts: { ..., GET:/products/STRING → POST:/cart/add : 1 }

t=5m  User calls  POST /checkout         deque: [POST:/cart/add]
                                          → emit transition  POST:/cart/add → POST:/checkout
                                          ...

t=10m ── WINDOW END ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
      currentAccumulator swapped to fresh one (new writes go here immediately)
      WindowSnapshot taken from old accumulator → sent async to WindowFlusher
      Per-user deques reset lazily on next access (no sweep needed)
```

### 10-minute window flip

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant K as Kafka records
    participant SA as SessionAnalyzer
    participant CA as CurrentAccumulator (Window N)
    participant NA as NewAccumulator (Window N+1)
    participant F as ApiSequencesFlusher

    K->>SA: process() calls stream in continuously

    Note over SA,CA: t = 0..10min, all writes go to Window N

    Note over SA: t = 10min — onWindowEnd() fires
    SA->>NA: create fresh accumulator
    SA-->>CA: volatile swap: currentAccumulator = NA
    Note over K,NA: new process() calls now write to Window N+1
    SA->>CA: snapshot(windowStart, windowEnd)
    SA->>F: CompletableFuture.runAsync → flush(snapshot)
    Note over F: async — hot path unblocked immediately

    F->>F: Build ApiSequences list\nfor each TransitionKey:\n  paths = [from.toString(), to.toString()]\n  transitionCount, prevStateCount, probability
    F->>DA: DataActor.writeApiSequences(List<ApiSequences>)
    DA->>DB: MongoDB bulkWrite $inc + $setOnInsert upsert\non (apiCollectionId, paths)

    Note over SA,NA: t = 10..20min, all writes go to Window N+1
```

### Flush payload → MongoDB \`api_sequences\`

Each flushed transition becomes an upsert keyed on \`(apiCollectionId, paths)\`:

```
apiCollectionId: 1234
paths: ["GET /products", "GET /products/STRING"]
transitionCount: 830        ← $inc (cumulative across windows)
prevStateCount:  1820       ← $inc (cumulative)
probability:     0.456      ← $set (latest window value)
lastUpdatedAt:   <epoch>    ← $set
createdAt:       <epoch>    ← $setOnInsert (only on first insert)
isActive:        true       ← $setOnInsert
```

---

## Module Structure

```
behaviour_modelling/
├── core/
│   ├── UserIdentifier.java      — extracts user identity from HttpResponseParams
│   ├── WindowAccumulator.java   — accumulates counts; userId param wired for phase-2 unique-user weighting
│   └── WindowFlusher.java       — receives completed WindowSnapshot at end of each window
├── model/
│   ├── TransitionKey.java       — ApiInfoKey[] sequence key with Arrays.equals/hashCode
│   ├── UserSessionState.java    — per-user Deque<ApiInfoKey>; lazily reset on window boundary
│   └── WindowSnapshot.java      — immutable Map<ApiInfoKey,Long> + Map<TransitionKey,Long>
├── impl/
│   ├── IpBasedIdentifier.java   — uses sourceIP as user identity
│   ├── RawCountAccumulator.java — ConcurrentHashMap<LongAdder> for concurrent hot-path increments
│   └── ApiSequencesFlusher.java — converts snapshot → List<ApiSequences> → DataActor.writeApiSequences()
├── SequenceAnalyzerConfig.java  — holds: sequenceLength, windowDurationMs, UserIdentifier,
│                                  Supplier<WindowAccumulator>, WindowFlusher, AktoPolicyNew
└── SessionAnalyzer.java         — orchestrator: process(), atomic window flip, async flush
```

**DataActor layer additions:**
- \`DataActor.writeApiSequences(List<ApiSequences>)\` — new abstract method
- \`DbActor.writeApiSequences\` — MongoDB \`$inc\` upsert via \`ApiSequencesDao\`
- \`ClientActor.writeApiSequences\` — HTTP POST to \`/writeApiSequences\` on database-abstractor

---

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit test \`RawCountAccumulator\`: concurrent increments produce correct counts
- [x] Unit test \`SessionAnalyzer.process()\`: transitions emitted correctly for 2-length sequences
- [x] Unit test window boundary: no cross-window transitions emitted
- [ ] Unit test templatization: raw numeric/UUID segments resolve to same \`ApiInfoKey\`
- [x] Integration: wire \`SessionAnalyzer\` into \`handleResponseParams\` and verify snapshot shape
- [x] Integration: \`ApiSequencesFlusher\` writes correct documents to \`api_sequences\` collection

## Summary
This PR adds a metrics monitoring page for Mini Runtime modules, following the same UI pattern as PR #4305 (Threat Detection metrics).

## Changes
- ✨ **New Component**: `MiniRuntimeMetrics.jsx` - Displays infrastructure metrics for Mini Runtime modules

- 🎨 **UI Updates**: Added "Mini Runtime" option to metrics navigation dropdown

- **Infrastructure Metrics Display**: Shows 3 key metrics:
  - CPU Usage Percentage
  - Heap Memory Used (MB)
  - Non-Heap Memory Used (MB)
- **System Info Display**: Extracts and displays from metrics API:
  - CPU Cores (Available Processors)
  - Max Heap Memory
  - Total Physical Memory
- **Multi-Instance Support**: Dropdown to filter by instance ID
- **Date Range Filtering**: Configurable time range for metrics
- **Empty State Handling**: Shows appropriate messages when no data exists

## Implementation Details
- Uses `moduleType: 'MINI_RUNTIME'` filter strategy
- Extracts system info from metrics API (latest values)
- No chart legends for cleaner single-instance view
- Follows same component structure as ModuleMetrics for consistency

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a major performance optimization for the threat detection system by implementing cursor-based pagination and migrating queries to use a new `actor_info` collection. The changes significantly improve query performance for listing threat actors by utilizing pre-aggregated data and efficient MongoDB indexing strategies.

## Key Changes

### Backend - Actor Info Collection & Pagination
**Files Modified:**
- `apps/threat-detection-backend/src/main/java/com/akto/threat/backend/db/ActorInfoModel.java`
  - Restructured model to support cursor-based pagination with MongoDB ObjectId
  - Added comprehensive fields: `actorId`, `filterId`, `category`, `apiCollectionId`, `url`, `method`, `country`, `severity`, `host`, `contextSource`, `discoveredAt`, `updatedAt`, `lastAttackTs`, `totalAttacks`, `status`, `isCritical`, `latestMetadata`
  - Maintained backward compatibility with existing `ip` and `updatedTs` fields
  - Added Lombok annotations for cleaner code

- `apps/threat-detection-backend/src/main/java/com/akto/threat/backend/dao/ActorInfoDao.java`
  - Added `createIndicesIfAbsent()` method to create optimized compound indexes
  - Created indexes for cursor pagination: `idx_lastAttackTs_id_desc`
  - Created indexes for query optimization:
    - `idx_lastAttackTs_contextSource_isCritical` (critical actors count)
    - `idx_lastAttackTs_contextSource_status` (active actors count)  
    - `idx_lastAttackTs_contextSource_country` (country grouping)
  - Removed redundant single-field `lastAttackTs` index to avoid query planner confusion

- `apps/threat-detection-backend/src/main/java/com/akto/threat/backend/service/ThreatActorService.java`
  - Implemented `listThreatActorsFromActorInfo()` with ObjectId-based cursor pagination
  - Optimized query filter building with timestamp-first filtering for better index utilization
  - Added `USE_ACTOR_INFO_TABLE` feature flag (env variable) to toggle between old and new implementation
  - Implemented efficient `fetchPaginatedActors()` method with proper error handling
  - Added comprehensive logging for performance monitoring

- `apps/threat-detection-backend/src/main/java/com/akto/threat/backend/service/MaliciousEventService.java`
  - Added `fetchThreatActorFiltersFromActorInfo()` for optimized filter queries using MongoDB `distinct()`
  - Feature-flagged filter fetching with `USE_ACTOR_INFO_TABLE`
  - Maintained backward compatibility with existing malicious events implementation

### Dashboard Backend
**Files Modified:**
- `apps/dashboard/src/main/java/com/akto/action/threat_detection/DashboardThreatActor.java`
  - Added `objectId` field to support cursor-based pagination
  - Updated constructor and added getter/setter methods

- `apps/dashboard/src/main/java/com/akto/action/threat_detection/ThreatActorAction.java`
  - Added `cursor` parameter for pagination
  - Updated `fetchThreatActors()` to pass cursor to backend service
  - Added getter/setter for cursor field

### Frontend - Web Dashboard
**Files Modified:**
- `apps/dashboard/web/polaris_web/web/src/apps/dashboard/pages/threat_detection/api.js`
  - Updated `fetchThreatActors()` to accept and conditionally include `cursor` parameter
  - Maintained backward compatibility by only sending cursor when provided

- `apps/dashboard/web/polaris_web/web/src/apps/dashboard/pages/threat_detection/components/ThreatActorsTable.jsx`
  - Added `lastCursor` state to track ObjectId for pagination
  - Updated pagination logic to use cursor when navigating to subsequent pages
  - Added `useEffect` hook to reset cursor when date range changes
  - Extracts and stores `objectId` from last row for next page cursor

### Initialization
**Files Modified:**
- `apps/threat-detection-backend/src/main/java/com/akto/threat/backend/dao/ThreatDetectionDaoInit.java`
  - Added `ActorInfoDao.instance.createIndicesIfAbsent(accountId)` call to ensure indexes are created on initialization

## Implementation Details

### Cursor-Based Pagination Strategy
- Uses MongoDB ObjectId for cursor-based pagination (ObjectId embeds timestamp in first 4 bytes)
- First page: skip=0, returns first N results
- Subsequent pages: cursor=last_seen_ObjectId, filters using `_id > cursor` (or `_id < cursor` for descending)
- Maintains consistent total count across pages by counting before applying cursor filter

### Query Optimization
- Filters applied in optimal order for index utilization:
  1. Timestamp range (leverages compound indexes)
  2. Attack type (filterId)
  3. Country
  4. Host
  5. Actor ID (deduplicated from multiple sources)
  6. Context source
- Uses MongoDB `distinct()` for efficient filter value fetching
- Compound indexes designed to support multiple query patterns

### Feature Flag Control
- `USE_ACTOR_INFO_TABLE` environment variable controls feature activation
- Defaults to `false` for backward compatibility
- Allows gradual rollout and easy rollback if needed

## Performance Benefits
- Eliminates slow aggregation queries on malicious_events collection
- Cursor-based pagination provides O(1) page navigation vs O(N) skip-based
- Pre-aggregated data in actor_info reduces query complexity
- Optimized compound indexes support multiple query patterns efficiently
- `distinct()` queries for filters are significantly faster than aggregations

- Remove activity fetching loop from `listThreatActors` to eliminate N+1 queries (was fetching 40 activities per actor, up to 50 actors = 51 total queries)
- Add new `fetchThreatsForActor` API endpoint for lazy-loading activity data on-demand
- Update frontend to fetch activity when user opens actor details panel (lazy loading)

## Changes
| Layer | File | Change |
|-------|------|--------|
| Proto | `service.proto` | Added `FetchThreatsForActorRequest` and `FetchThreatsForActorResponse` messages |
| Backend | `ThreatActorService.java` | Added `fetchThreatsForActor()` method, removed N+1 loop from `listThreatActors()` |
| Backend | `DashboardRouter.java` | Added `/fetch_threats_for_actor` endpoint |
| Dashboard | `ThreatActorAction.java` | Added action method and `actorActivities` field |
| Dashboard | `DashboardThreatActor.java` | Removed `activity` field (now fetched separately) |
| Dashboard | `struts.xml` | Added action mapping |
| Frontend | `api.js` | Added `fetchThreatsForActor()` function |
| Frontend | `ActorDetails.jsx` | Fetch activity on mount with loading state |
| Frontend | `ActivityLog.jsx` | Handle loading state with spinner |

## Performance Impact
- **Before**: 51 queries for 50 actors (~500-1000ms)
- **After**: 1 query for 50 actors (~50-100ms) + lazy load per actor expansion

Add bulk severity update feature with persistence across test runs
body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive severity management features to the Testing Results and Issues pages:

1. **Bulk Severity Update in Testing Results Page**: Users can now select multiple test results and update their severity in bulk
2. **Manual Severity Persistence**: When users manually change an issue's severity, that preference is preserved across future test runs
3. **Immediate UI Updates**: Severity badges update instantly after changes without requiring page refresh

## Changes

### Backend Changes

**IssuesAction.java**
- Added `bulkUpdateIssueSeverityFromTestResults()` method to handle bulk severity updates from test results
- Implements incremental update for `TestingRunResultSummary.countIssues` to efficiently track severity counts
- Updates severity in three collections:
  - `testing_run_issues` (main issue tracking)
  - `testing_run_result` and `vulnerable_testing_run_result` (test result confidence)
  - `testing_run_result_summaries` (count tracking)

**TestExecutor.java**
- Added logic to check for user's manual severity preferences before creating new test results
- Queries `TestingRunIssues` collection for existing manual updates
- Applies user's preferred severity to new test results if found
- Logs when user preferences override template-detected severities

**TestingIssuesHandler.java**
- Modified to preserve manual severity updates when tests re-run
- Checks `lastUpdatedBy` field to detect user modifications
- Prevents automatic overwriting of user's preferred severities

**struts.xml**
- Added new API endpoint: `api/bulkUpdateIssueSeverityFromTestResults`

### Frontend Changes

**SingleTestRunPage.js**
- Added "Update severity" bulk action to test results table
- Integrated `SeverityUpdateModal` component
- Added handlers for bulk severity updates with success/error toasts

**TestRunResultFlyout.jsx**
- Fixed issue where severity badge wasn't updating immediately after change
- Updates `issueDetails.severity` directly and triggers re-render using `refreshFlag`

**api.js**
- Added `bulkUpdateIssueSeverityFromTestResults()` API wrapper

## Test Plan

- [x] Select multiple test results and bulk update severity
- [x] Verify severity updates in UI immediately
- [x] Run same test again and verify user's severity preference is preserved
- [x] Check backend logs for severity override messages
- [x] Verify counts update correctly in summaries
- [x] Test individual severity update in Issue Details flyout
- [x] Verify severity badge updates immediately without page refresh

## Technical Details

### Incremental Count Updates
Instead of recalculating all issue counts from scratch, the implementation uses incremental arithmetic:
- Fetches old severities before updating
- Calculates delta: `old severity count - 1`, `new severity count + 1`
- Applies changes efficiently without fetching all issues

### Severity Persistence Logic
1. User manually changes issue severity → `lastUpdatedBy` field is set
2. Next test run → `TestExecutor` checks for existing issue with `lastUpdatedBy`
3. If found → applies user's preferred severity instead of template's detected severity
4. `TestingIssuesHandler` preserves the severity during updates

In-Memory Only)] J[(Count-Min Sketch
Synced to Redis)] end B -.-> I D -.-> I E -.-> J ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Sliding Window - 5 minutes M1[Min 1
